- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed with sharp drops, model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.33 → 1.00 → 0.33), model fails to mean-revert; apply a 1–3% downward bias to prevent prolonged overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends in low-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment <0.4.
- If sentiment is high and price is falling, model may misread trend; apply a 1–2% upward bias to counteract sentiment-driven overcorrection.
- Model tends to lag in early days of sentiment shifts; for 1–3 day horizons, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment turns positive after 2–3 days.
